name: Robot Digital Prototype
promise: Prove one robot behavior in a deterministic digital prototype and expose the sim-to-real gap.
summary: A bounded behavior contract, the minimum active robot modules, deterministic scenario evidence, falsification, and an honest digital-only receipt.
useWhen: A robot concept needs one behavior demonstrated before fabrication or commissioning.
Simulation can retire a named mechanical, control, planning, or interface uncertainty.
notFor: A passive object or simple mechanism that only needs Mechanical CAD Review.
A requirement to model every robot subsystem regardless of the behavior being tested.

skills.name: Text to CAD

workstreams.name: Behavior and environment contract
workstreams.brief: Define one observable behavior, environment, success threshold, failing scenarios, assumptions, and digital boundary.

workstreams.name: Minimum digital prototype
workstreams.brief: Build only the geometry, dynamics, controller, interfaces, and scenarios needed by the behavior and active modules.

workstreams.name: Deterministic challenge
workstreams.brief: Repeat nominal and failing scenarios, inspect the model, quantify uncertainty, and publish the sim-to-real gap.

guardrails: Do not claim physical safety, durability, manufacturability, calibration, or real-world performance from simulation.
Do not add subsystems merely to resemble a complete robot.
Do not command physical equipment or deploy robot software without separate approval.
Preserve units, frames, solver settings, seeds, and asset provenance.
Digitally proven means the contracted behavior passes reproducibly in the declared model; it never means a physical robot is safe, buildable, or commissioned.
verification: Replay nominal and intentionally failing scenarios from a clean environment.
Challenge the behavior threshold across named perturbations.
Inspect active-module interfaces and report numerical or modeling instability.
List every assumption that requires physical evidence.
Lock one behavior and its falsifiable threshold.
Build the smallest executable model with fixed units, frames, solver settings, and seeds.
Run active-module challenges plus at least one negative scenario.
Separate digital evidence from every claim that still needs physical proof.

expectations.statement: The digital prototype reproducibly performs one contracted behavior.
The scenario suite detects at least one intentionally failing condition.
The receipt states what simulation cannot establish.
Active geometry and interfaces support the simulated behavior. Applicable when: Geometry, joints, collision, or physical interfaces materially determine the behavior.
The locomotion model meets the behavior threshold under named terrain conditions. Applicable when: The behavior requires a mobile base or legged motion.
The manipulation model reaches and controls the named task. Applicable when: The behavior requires reaching, grasping, or tool interaction.
Planning state and failure semantics are explicit and exercised. Applicable when: The behavior requires sequencing, planning, or explicit recovery states.
The selected ROS 2 interface is coherent and testable. Applicable when: ROS 2 interoperability is an explicit requirement.
The selected perception model is tested against named uncertainty. Applicable when: The behavior depends on estimated rather than ground-truth state.
The selected learned controller is reproducible and bounded. Applicable when: A learned policy is essential to the behavior under test.

Robot digital prototype produces enough evidence for an independent readiness decision. The possible decisions are digitally-proven, repair-required, no-go. Digitally proven means the contracted behavior passes reproducibly in the declared model; it never means a physical robot is safe, buildable, or commissioned.
failureModes: missing evidence for the declared outcome
decision made from assumptions or unverified claims
